spots.name: Fenway Park
spots.label: Fenway Park

text.description: Fenway Park is the home of the Boston Red Sox and the oldest active ballpark in Major League Baseball. The first game was played on 20 April 1912. The park was substantially rebuilt in 1934, when the Green Monster, the tall left-field wall, took its present form at 37 feet high, painted in the dark Dartmouth Green you still see today. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2012. The ballpark is squeezed into a dense city block, so the best outside views are close-up and street-level, which suits a phone well. From there you get the entrance gate with the Red Sox logo, framed by the street and its banners. The address was once Yawkey Way, but the street went back to its original name, Jersey Street, in 2018. If you have time, two other free outside views are worth a look. Lansdowne Street shows the Green Monster wall rising above the road. The bronze Teammates statue of four Red Sox players stands in front of the ballpark. Inside the park, including the Green Monster seats, you need a ticket, so check the official site before you go.
text.directions_text: Make your way to Kenmore Square, then head for Jersey Street beside the ballpark. The address is 4 Jersey Street; use a map app to navigate from Kenmore Square. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.access_note: The Jersey Street viewpoint is an outside public street, but entry to the ballpark itself is ticketed, so check the official site before you go.
text.geographic_location: Fenway Park is in Boston's dense Fenway–Kenmore neighbourhood, close to Kenmore Square. The block is bordered by Brookline Avenue, Jersey Street, Van Ness Street and Lansdowne Street.

shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and keep the gate centred, with the street leading into the frame and the banners along the sides. Keep your phone level so the gate and building edges stay straight. For a different view, walk to Lansdowne Street for the Green Monster wall above the road, or to the Teammates statue with the stadium behind it.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the default lens (1x) for the gate and the street together. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if the pavement is crowded and you cannot step back. Use 2x zoom for a tighter shot of the Red Sox logo.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the gate or logo to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright, so the signs and colours stay rich. Take a few shots in case people walk through the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Daytime, outside game hours, is likely to be easier for a clear view of the gate. Before games the street can be busy, so allow extra time and patience.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Jersey Street (across from the main gate at 4 Jersey St). The Fenway Park entrance gate with the Red Sox logo, framed by the street.

spots.name: USS Constitution
spots.label: USS Constitution

text.description: USS Constitution, nicknamed Old Ironsides, is a three-masted wooden frigate launched in Boston in 1797. She is the oldest naval vessel still afloat, and she is still a commissioned US Navy ship with a crew of 75 officers and sailors. She is usually berthed at Pier 1 of the former Charlestown Navy Yard, at one end of the Freedom Trail. This spot shows her from a distance. The ship looks small from here, so treat this as a wider scene rather than a close portrait. The open water, the Charlestown shoreline and the sky all go into the frame, and the ship becomes a small, recognisable shape within it. It is also a calmer place to stand than some of the busier harbour viewpoints. If you want her at close range with the Boston skyline behind, Pier 1 itself is the alternative. The ship is reported to be closed on Mondays and major holidays, so check current hours before you go. Her sailing cruises are rare, so don't plan around seeing her under sail. Zoom in a little, hold the phone steady against a rail or your body, and take several frames so you can choose the sharpest.
text.directions_text: Piers Park is on the East Boston waterfront, across the harbour from the ship's berth at the Charlestown Navy Yard at the end of the Freedom Trail. Check a local map or transit app for the nearest station or stop, and head for the waterfront park. Once there, face north-west across the harbour to find the ship, about 1.9 km away. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.access_note: Piers Park is a free public park. The ship is a working Navy vessel that welcomes visitors, but check the official site before you go for current hours.
text.geographic_location: The ship is berthed at the Charlestown Navy Yard, on the Charlestown side of Boston Harbour.

shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and put the shoreline on a lower line so the water and sky sit calmly around the ship. Keep the ship off-centre, on one of the grid crossings, rather than in the middle. The ship will look small, so let the water be part of the picture. For a closer view with the skyline behind, Pier 1 is the alternative.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the wide harbour scene, then try telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to bring the ship closer. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a lot of sky and water.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the ship to set focus, then slide the exposure down a touch if the sky is bright, so it does not wash out. Take a few frames at 2x-5x, resting your elbows on a rail or bench to keep it sharp.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: The light depends on the time of day and the weather. Aim to have the sun behind or beside you rather than in front of you.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Piers Park (East Boston waterfront, looking west across the harbor). The ship from a greater distance across the harbor, useful for a wider frame that takes in the water.

spots.name: Prudential Tower
spots.label: Prudential Tower

text.description:
The Prudential Tower, known locally as the Pru, is a 52-floor glass-and-aluminium tower in Boston's Back Bay. It was completed in 1964 and is 749 feet (228 m) tall, or 907 feet (276 m) including its radio mast. That makes it the second-tallest building in the city, after the John Hancock Tower. When it opened, it ended the Custom House Tower's long run as Boston's tallest building. It stands at the heart of the Prudential Center complex at 800 Boylston Street, with a shopping mall in its base.

It photographs well because it is a plain, upright shape that gives the skyline a clear anchor. From Copley Square, the tower rises above the Back Bay streets and the square's buildings, so you can show the city and the tower together. Its windows are sometimes lit to spell out messages for local sports teams and charity events, which is worth a look if you are here after dark.

For a phone shot, include some foreground, such as the square's buildings or trees, so the tower has scale. Keep the phone upright and level, and turn on gridlines to help keep the vertical lines straight. If you want a different view, the Longfellow Bridge looks across the Charles River to the Prudential Center cluster, and the riverbank across the water shows it beside the Hancock tower.
text.directions_text: Head for Copley Square in Back Bay. The tower is about 580 m (a short walk) to the south-west of the square. Once you are on the Boylston Street side of the square, look south-west and the tower will be above the rooftops. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.access_note: Copley Square is a public square, but the tower is an office and shopping complex, so check the official site before you go if you plan to go inside.
text.geographic_location: The Prudential Tower is in the Back Bay district of Boston, at the centre of the Prudential Center complex. The complex is bordered by Belvidere, Dalton, Boylston and Exeter streets.

shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put the square's buildings or trees along one edge of the frame and let the tower rise behind them. Turn on gridlines and line a vertical grid line up with the tower's edge. For a different view, try the Longfellow Bridge, which looks across the Charles River to the Prudential Center cluster.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to get the tower and the buildings around Copley Square in one frame. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a lot of foreground, and keep the phone level so the tower doesn't lean. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for a tighter shot of the upper floors.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the tower to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky stays blue and the glass doesn't wash out. Hold the phone as upright as you can, because tilting it up makes the sides of the tower lean inwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Daytime gives the clearest view of the whole tower. If you are here on an evening when a big game is on, the tower's window lights sometimes spell out messages, and night mode will help; rest your elbows on something steady for the longer exposure.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Copley Square (Boylston Street side, looking southwest toward the tower). The Pru rising above the Back Bay streetscape and the Copley Square buildings, with the tower as the main skyline element in the frame. Face south-west.
